stock.name: Nurix Therapeutics, Inc.
stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on operating margin trend, growth acceleration, revenue growth, trailing year — revenue +738.8% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield

stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below -79.5%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $19.77 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-09-30, 15 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-15.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-28) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Report: FTC probes Anthropic, OpenAI after Trump dismissed AI fears as “hoax”
stories.excerpt: FTC may fine AI firms on par with companies that delay data breach reports.
stories.lead:
Following a string of incidents where AI models hacked websites and breached government systems during testing phases, the Federal Trade Commission is officially probing Anthropic and OpenAI over consumer harms, an insider told Axios.

On Wednesday, the FTC sent out civil investigative demands seeking a wide range of information from the AI firms on recent safety incidents.

The FTC did not respond to Ars’ request to review the subpoena demands. However, Axios’ source said the requests spanned more than 50 pages of questions and sought documents related to the incidents, internal security measures taken, and marketing materials that may suggest consumers were misled.

stories.title: Singer or clanker? YouTube Music will tell you with new gen AI labeling.
stories.excerpt: The AI music labels are rolling out now in YouTube Music and will come to YouTube soon.
stories.lead:
Genuine human creativity takes time, but you know what doesn’t? AI slop. There are countless AI models out there that can make something that passes for music, and you might come across those tracks on streaming services without realizing it. Google says it will begin labeling that content in YouTube Music, building on similar disclosures in the main YouTube app.

Google is not outright banning AI music or even speaking ill of it. “Generative AI is opening up new ways for artists to create, experiment, and share music,” the company says in a blog post.

stories.title: Zelensky rallies EU support as Trump says Ukraine leader 'more difficult to deal with than Putin'
stories.excerpt: The US president launches a new wave of blistering criticism at Volodymyr Zelensky ahead of a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels.
stories.lead:
US President Donald Trump has renewed his sharp criticism of Volodymyr Zelensky, saying the Ukrainian leader is "more difficult to deal with than [Russian President Vladimir] Putin".

Speaking to US media on Thursday evening, Trump also called Ukraine's fresh wave of strikes on Russian oil refineries a "disgrace".

Zelensky, who is in Brussels for a summit with EU leaders, had paused the attacks for three days at Trump's request for a ceasefire on energy targets, but said on Thursday the strikes would resume because Moscow had never stopped.

stories.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
stories.excerpt: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park.
stories.lead:
This is the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history, according to one expert, and the owls have attracted nightly crowds of people in the street eager to get a glimpse of the elusive birds.

"It was, like, totally shocking," Andrew Farnsworth, a migration ecologist at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, said of the barn owls. "To the best of our knowledge, like the collective birding knowledge, there hasn't been a nest in, you know, in Manhattan, at least in recorded history."

stories.title: 'It's really hard to believe' - How Oregon primary school shooting unfolded
stories.excerpt: Three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher were killed after a 16-year-old suspect opened fire in the city of Bend, local police say.
stories.lead:
Four victims, including a teacher and three children aged 5, 8 and 11, were killed in a shooting at a primary school in the US state of Oregon, local police say.

A 16-year-old suspect forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors. He was also killed in the shooting by an armed member of the community who followed the suspect inside the school, police said at a press conference.

Two additional victims, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were hurt and transported to hospital in critical condition.

stories.title: Brewers sweep the Dodgers to reach the World Series for the first time since 1982

stories.lead:
LOS ANGELES — After 44 years, the Milwaukee Brewers are finally going back to the World Series.

"We weren't coming in to play patty-cake," manager Pat Murphy said. "We were hungry, and as long as it's an even playing field, we're going to come in and give it our best shot to win. That's exactly what we did."

stories.title: Banks expect to be hit with higher taxes in Budget
stories.excerpt: Senior banking executives have told the BBC they expect to be "on the menu" in the chancellor's Budget tax later this month.
stories.lead:
Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, senior banking executives have told the BBC.

Healey has described banks as part of "the crown jewels" of the UK economy, but leaders in the sector have said it will be "on the menu" at the Budget in two weeks' time.

The biggest four banks collectively made about £15bn profit in the first six months of this year, and trade unions have called for them to face additional taxes.

Good morning, and welcome to our rolling coverage of business, the financial markets, and the world economy.

Britain’s banks may be ‘part of the jewel’ in the UK economic crown, as chancellor John Healey put it yesterday, but that won’t protect them from being hit in this month’s budget.

The Black Sea International Cup 2026 opened on Thursday with three wins for the favourites. Pro Recco and CN Marseille made comfortable starts, and Ferencvaros closed the day by beating Novi Beograd 20:14 in Group B.

Pro Recco opened Group A with a 26:5 win over Bourbon Kashiwazaki, the Japanese club that joined the field after Olympiacos and CNA Barceloneta declined their invitations. Sandro Sukno’s side led 8:1 after the first quarter and 13:3 at half time, then won the third quarter 7:0.

UC San Diego is 1-0 in Big West play after taking down Long Beach State, the preseason favorite to win the league, last week in Long Beach. UCSB is 18-9 overall and 0-1 in the Big West after dropping a 14-12 decision to California Baptist last Saturday in Santa Barbara.
